about: Cited protein and energy ranges (ADR-048, Amendment 2). Loaded by services/api/app/nutrition.py; bodycomp.py checks its calorie bands against this file at import. Every number below was read in the source's own text on 2026-11-02; `sources` says how much of each paper. The energy reviews address natural bodybuilders, not the general public, so applying them to recreational lifters is our extrapolation; the app's own calorie limits (docs/privacy-and-safety.md) are stricter, are not derived from these papers, and override the cited ranges.

morton-2018.read: Results and most of the Discussion verbatim; the end of the Discussion and the Conclusion not read verbatim

issn-protein-2017.read: whole article body verbatim; references not read

helms-2014.tbd_after_demo: read the tail (kept in the plan, not deleted)

iraki-2019.tbd_after_demo: read the tail (kept in the plan, not deleted)

protein.label: typical range
protein.unit: g per kg of total body weight per day
protein.applies_when: body weight is known (grams = range x weight_kg); no range is shown without it

also_listed.text: One position stand lists 1.4-2.0 g per kg per day as sufficient for most exercising people.

protein.basis: Morton 2018: gains in fat-free mass plateaued at 1.62 g/kg/day (95% CI 1.03 to 2.20; not statistically significant, p = 0.079); the authors call about 2.2 a pragmatic estimate. Iraki 2019: 'sufficient protein (1.6-2.2 g/kg/day)'. ISSN 2017 gives 1.4-2.0 g/kg/day, overlapping this range.

locators.issn-protein-2017: Abstract, position statement; 'Recommended intake' key points

protein.agent_text: A typical protein range for people who lift weights is about 1.6 to 2.2 grams per kilogram of total body weight per day (one position stand lists 1.4 to 2.0). It is an average from research, not a personal prescription.

protein_per_meal.note: The sources differ, so no single number is prescribed: Iraki 2019 gives 0.40-0.55 g/kg per meal over 3-6 meals; ISSN 2017 gives about 0.25 g/kg or 20-40 g per dose, every 3-4 hours.

energy.label: typical range
energy.population: natural bodybuilders (off-season gaining phase; contest-preparation loss phase)

locators.iraki-2019: Section 2 'Positive Energy Balance'; Abstract (gain rate). Section 2 also writes the gain rate as '0.25-0.5 kg per week', inconsistent with the abstract's % of bodyweight; the abstract is used

bulk.reason: The app caps a surplus at 10% of daily needs (privacy-and-safety.md); the cited 10-20% is for bodybuilders. The app's cap overrides the cited range.

cut.reason: The cited loss quantity is a weekly rate of body weight (0.5-1%/week), not a percentage of maintenance. The deficit band is the app's own design limit; the weekly rate is enforced by the 1%/week cap checked against the cited range.

recomp.reason: No cited counterpart; the app's own band.

maintain.reason: No cited counterpart; the app's own band.

energy.note: Advanced lifters should aim for the lower end of the surplus or be more conservative (Iraki 2019); no numeric advanced rate is given.

planner_rules.protein_point_pick: not allowed: the planner shows the whole cited range and does not pick a value inside it, unless a rule is added and labelled as OUR rule, not a cited number
planner_rules.loss_rate_scaling_by_leanness: not allowed: the weekly loss cap is not scaled by leanness, unless a rule is added and labelled as OUR rule, not a cited number

not_used.reason: For lean, resistance-trained people during an energy deficit. The two papers state the unit differently (the ISSN abstract per kg body weight, Helms per kg of lean body mass) and we do not know the user's lean mass. Not prescribed; a later decision.

tbd_after_demo.what: For a high BMI, show the per-kg range without a computed total. The BMI threshold is OUR rule, not a cited number, and is labelled as such. Until then the total is computed from total body weight for everyone.

safety_text: If you have kidney disease or any other medical condition, talk to a doctor or dietitian before changing your protein or calorie intake. This is not medical advice.
